title: Error.text() writes string payloads as Okkama literals: quotes, backslashes, controls, nested variants
purpose: Observe that an error's text is unambiguous and source-compatible (#306).

stdout.text:
Ferr.text("a \"q\"\n")
Ferr.text("back\\slash\ttab\rcr\u{1b}esc\u{7f}del")
Ferr.text("é😀 ok")
Ferr.pair("x\", \"y", "z")
Ferr.nested(Inner.named("in\"ner\n"))
Ferr.plain Ferr.text("")

provenance.origin: authored for #306 from the owner's decision
provenance.expected_basis: owner decision on #306: a string payload is written in Okkama string literal syntax (backslash, quote, newline, tab and carriage return escaped, other control characters as \u{hex}, printable Unicode unchanged), recursively in nested error variants.
